description: Somos Los Jedi de la NASA, un grupo de verdaderos apasionados por el espacio, la ciencia ficción y la tecnología que vive con la cabeza en las estrellas y el corazón en la galaxia. Combinamos nuestra fascinación por el universo, el coleccionismo, la ingeniería y los sables de luz con habilidades sólidas en análisis de datos, desarrollo de software, diseño creativo y resolución de problemas complejos.
summary:
SPATIUM is a 2D space rescue video game developed by team Los Jedi de la NASA. Players act as NASA astronauts who repair their ship through mini-games, manage resources, rescue crew members, and send expeditions to other planets to collect materials. An onboard 3D printer turns those materials into new parts and space station modules.

The game addresses the challenge by making space mission design accessible and engaging. Every planet offers materials that really exist there, and the cybersecurity missions use real NASA information, so players learn real science while making mission decisions. Between days, a "Did you know?" screen shares NASA facts.

It matters because many young people see space science as distant and difficult. By turning real data into decisions, SPATIUM makes learning feel like an adventure and inspires the next generation of explorers, engineers, and cybersecurity defenders.
details:
SPATIUM is a 2D browser game for the Space Mission Design Game challenge. The player is a NASA astronaut on a rescue mission. Each day is a chapter: the player repairs ship systems through minigames (a retro arcade defense against a cyberattack, leak patching, engine calibration and valve sequences), manages fuel, water, electricity and budget, rescues stranded astronauts, and sends crew members on 24‑hour expeditions to other worlds to collect materials. An onboard 3D printer turns those materials into repair kits and space station modules. Random events, a traveling space trader and consequence-driven choices make every playthrough different.

Learning with real data. The materials of each world are based on real findings: iron oxides on Mars, water ice and carbon compounds on Ceres (NASA's Dawn mission), aluminum, titanium and silicon in lunar regolith, and sulfur and polar ice on Mercury (MESSENGER). 3D printing in space reflects the printer operating on the ISS since 2014. The cyberattack minigame teaches real facts about phishing and malware threats reported against NASA, and "Did you know?" loading screens share NASA curiosities.

Benefits and impact. Players learn space science, resource planning and basic cybersecurity by playing. We want to make STEM approachable for Spanish-speaking students and inspire future mission designers and station builders.

Tools. HTML, CSS and vanilla JavaScript (Canvas for minigames, browser storage for saves), Visual Studio Code, and GitHub Pages for hosting. Playable on computers and phones.

Creativity. We combine resource management, arcade minigames, visual-novel dialogues, original characters and story, and a mechanic where real planetary materials build a space station.

Factors we considered. Scientific accuracy, scarce resources with real consequences, short and clear dialogues, playability on any device, and a game fully in Spanish.
